t: Section 1010(d)(6) of the Controlled Substances Import and Export Act (21 U.S.C. 960(d)(6)) is amended to read as follows:“(6) imports a listed chemical in violation of section 1002, imports or exports such a chemical in violation of section 1007 or 1018, or transfers such a chemical in violation of section 1018(d); or”.

fable.w: This section only amends a criminal penalty provision that defines prohibited import, export and transfer conduct for listed chemicals. It contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. There is no real tempting reading, because nothing in it brings a non-federal party into a federal decision.
fable.s: imports a listed chemical in violation of section 1002, imports or exports such a chemical in violation of section 1007 or 1018, or transfers such a chemical in violation of section 1018(d)

qwen_block.w: This section amends a criminal statute to define specific violations related to the import, export, or transfer of listed chemicals. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings before a federal decision is made. It is purely a substantive legal definition of prohibited conduct.
qwen_block.s: Section 1010(d)(6) of the Controlled Substances Import and Export Act (21 U.S.C. 960(d)(6)) is amended to read as follows:“(6) imports a listed chemical in violation of section 1002, imports or exports such a chemical in violation of section 1007 or 1018, or transfers such a chemical in violation of section 1018(d); or”.

opus.w: This amendment only redefines the criminal offenses for importing, exporting or transferring listed chemicals in violation of other sections. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard or given a role in any federal decision. The references to imports and transfers describe banned conduct, not a participation process.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** Words like "imports," "exports," and "transfers," plus the cross-references to other sections, might look like regulated activity that involves outside parties. That reading doesn't hold up. The amendment only redefines what counts as a criminal violation involving listed chemicals. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a criminal statute to define specific violations related to the import, export, or transfer of listed chemicals. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside parties (such as the public, states, or companies) before making a decision. It simply establishes legal prohibitions and penalties. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1010(d)(6) of the Controlled Substances Import and Export Act (21 U.S.C. 960(d)(6)) is amended to read as follows:“(6) imports a listed chemical in violation of section 1002, imports or exports such a chemical in violation of section 1007 or 1018, or transfers such a chemical in violation of section 1018(d); or”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this section amends a statute regulating imports and exports, it implicitly involves interaction with companies or individuals who import chemicals. However, the text itself only defines a criminal violation; it does not establish a process for public comment, consultation, or advisory input before a decision is made. The definition of participation requires the government to consult or coordinate with outsiders *before* making a decision, or to grant rights to sue/object. This section merely sets out the conditions for a legal violation.
